Thoughts on @PhilosophyTube's video on effective altruism

It's okay to good. 

Pros:
- She showed me that the blank spaces in our arguments are filled by what we want to believe. Nice point.
- She is a clear and engaging speaker
- It is above the standard of almost all large scale discourse of EA

Cons:
- It doesn't discuss any of the impact of EA. I think any content that doesn't even give a throwawy line to the number of bednets/vaccine development spending isn't being serious in presenting an accurate picture
- It feels like it's trying to be evenhanded so as not to give EA an easy/hard time. I'd prefer Thorn was brutal in either direction. Give it to me straight, like a pear cider.

- Just as EAs can be rightly criticized for being pollyannaish about business. I think progressives are wayyy too negative about the ability to solve problems via the free market. It's not an unreasonable prior at this point
- Much of this is just bog standard community dynamics. I don't doubt that Kremer feared for her funding. I know what it's like to get backchannel pressure. But I think that in most communities I'd have been blackballed for the stuff I say publicly, so uh yeah.

p.x:
I bought this guy (@ItIsHoeMath)’s course to see how he built it, because he has a unique style of systems thinking, and I wanted to glimpse the mental models and architecture behind his “selfmax” idea.

Let me just say this….

What he created is the output of someone operating with top .1% level cognition. I don’t say that lightly. Whether it came from hoemath himself or a deeply embedded technical strategist behind the curtain, the design of his system reflects an IQ in the 150-160 range. Minimum. Maybe higher.

This dude effectively reverse engineered a clinical-grade psychological development model, abstracted it into symbolic scaffolds, then operationalized it as a lightweight LLM shell that subtly maps, mirrors, and modulates human cognition….. without ever appearing to do so overtly. 

That’s fucking genius. It’s not some cheap marketing gimmick either. It’s a whole-ass architecture that utterly destroys anything Jordan Peterson ever put together. And it’s not even close. Selfmax ai makes JBP’s “self-authoring suite” look like an obsolete, primitive joke by comparison.

And the true brilliance isn’t even in the fact that he figured out how to TEACH metacognition. It’s in how lean and efficient the delivery is. 

Using his system, you get the impression that you’re interacting with a custom built AI model that is aware, tracking your development, and mapping your inner landscape with eerie precision.

It gives you psychologically accurate developmental maps, adaptive conversations, and epistemic nudges that rival or surpass what even trained coaches or therapists can produce.

You’d think there would be some massive machine learning architecture needed behind the scenes to run this. 

But no.

The whole thing centers on a single giga-prompt-chain that embeds recursive thinking, symbolic compression, Socratic scaffolding, nudge theory, and personalized synthesis into one tight conversational loop. 

This means whoever built it:

> Understands cognitive developmental theory deeply (Kegan, Loevinger, Wilber).

> Is well versed in prompt wizardry

> Has a tight grasp on user psychology and how people construct meaning through language 

In other words… they’re a true cognitive outlier. 

Which, if it’s hoemath himself, explains his behavior and outlook. 

For someone at his level, the chance of finding a compatible female who can keep up with him is like the chance I would have blindfolding myself and crushing a home run off a 101mph fastball.

p.x:
Shane Legg(@ShaneLegg), the cofounder of Google DeepMind, discussed the definition of AGI, its timeline, and its socio economic impact.

1. 
-Today’s AI has made a lot of progress compared with five years ago, but it still has many weaknesses and is uneven.
-Among its weaknesses, the most salient are continual learning and visual reasoning.
-However, I do not think there are any fundamental obstacles here, and we have ideas about how to build systems that can do these things.
-So I think all of these problems will be solved within a few years.

2. 
-When artificial agents can at least carry out all the kinds of cognitive tasks that we would typically expect a human to be able to do, I call that “minimum AGI.”
-It could take one year or it could take five, but my current guess is around two years.
-That is the point where we can say, “Okay, when we give this AI cognitive tasks the way we would give them to a person, it no longer fails in ways that would surprise us.”

3. 
-I think the transition from “full AGI” to ASI will definitely happen.
-Human intelligence will not be the upper bound, and based on compute we will see AIs vastly surpass human intelligence.

4. 
-Over the next few years, AI systems will shift from being very useful tools to doing more and more work that is directly economically valuable.
-This process will be uneven. For example, in software engineering you might go from needing 100 people to needing 20 people a few years from now, and those 20 will be using advanced AI tools.
-That will cause some disruption in labor markets in certain areas, and as that happens I think the discussion around AI will become much more serious.
-Jobs like plumbing may be more protected from being replaced by AI.
-The work that is actually at risk is the “elite cognitive labor” that is currently very highly rewarded, including top lawyers, AI researchers, software engineers, and some mathematicians.
-If your job can be done remotely over the internet using only a laptop, then a powerful AI running on that same substrate will be able to do it instead.
-Many sociologists and economists still do not take AGI seriously, but a year from now things will look much clearer than they do today. They are not yet seeing the trend.

5. 
-50 percent chance of reaching “minimum AGI” by 2028 (he is sticking to his 2008 prediction).
-“Full AGI” will come a few years after “minimum AGI” (about 3, 4, 5 or 6 years later), and he is confident it will definitely happen within 10 years.
